translations.text: Those counted from the tribe of Reuben were forty-six thousand five hundred.

And the sons of Simeon, according to their families, their divisions, and their ancestral houses, by the number of their names, counted individually: every male twenty years old and over who went out to serve in the army.
Those counted from the tribe of Judah were seventy-four thousand six hundred.

And the sons of Joseph, the sons of Ephraim, according to their families, their divisions, and their ancestral houses, by the number of their names, counted individually: every male twenty years old and over who went out to serve in the army.
And behold, I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites. They shall be their ransom, and the Levites shall be mine.

For every firstborn is mine. On the day when I struck down every firstborn in the land of the Egyptians, I consecrated to myself every firstborn in Israel, from humans to livestock. They shall be mine, for I am the Lord.
Take a census of the sons of Levi according to their ancestral houses, their divisions, and their families. You shall count every male one month old and over.
From the firstborn of the Israelites, he took the silver: one thousand three hundred sixty-five shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
Count the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi, according to their divisions and their ancestral houses.
They shall put a blue leather covering over it, spread an entirely blue cloth over it on top, and insert its carrying poles.

They shall put on it the utensils with which they minister at it: the censers, the meat forks, the basins, the covers, and all the utensils of the altar. They shall spread a blue leather covering over it and pass its carrying poles through it. They shall take a purple cloth and cover the basin and its bases, spread blue leather over it, and place it on the carrying poles.
This shall be the service of the division of Gershon in entering the tent and carrying loads.
From twenty-five years old and over, up to fifty years old: everyone who entered into the work of the holy things and the work of carrying the tabernacle of testimony.
Those included in the census were eight thousand five hundred eighty, according to the word of the Lord.
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: If any man's wife goes astray and treats him with contempt,
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:

The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed concerning a person, and he shall consecrate his head on that day.
The priest shall present them before the Lord and offer his sin offering and his burnt offering.
And the leaders of Israel brought offerings: the twelve leaders of their ancestral houses. They were the leaders of the tribes, and they were in charge of the census.
And he gave four carts and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, according to their service, under the direction of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
And one male goat as a sin offering.
And for the sacrifice of well-being, two heifers, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Elizaphan the son of Deuel.

His offerings: one silver basin weighing one hundred thirty units, one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering.
This is the rite for the dedication of the altar on the day when it was anointed, from the leaders of the Israelites: twelve silver basins, twelve silver bowls, and twelve boxes.
Take the Levites from among the Israelites and purify them.
And I took the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons of Israel.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
There were men who were unclean because of a human corpse and could not celebrate the Passover on that day. They came before Moses and Aaron on that day.
When the cloud remains from evening until morning, if the cloud rises in the morning, they shall set out, whether by day or by night. But if the cloud does not rise, they shall not set out.
If the cloud lingers for a month and overshadows it, the Israelites shall remain encamped and shall not set out.

You shall sound the second trumpet alarm, and the camps encamped on the south shall set out. You shall sound the third trumpet alarm, and the camps encamped on the west shall set out. You shall sound the fourth trumpet alarm, and the camps encamped on the north shall set out. They shall sound a trumpet alarm when they set out.
And the Israelites set out with their households from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Paran.
And over the army of the tribe of Benjamin was Abidan son of Gideoni.
And he said to him, “Do not leave us, for you were with us in the wilderness, and you shall be an elder among us.”
And the mixed multitude among them had a craving, and the Israelites sat down and wept, saying, “Who will give us meat to eat?”
And the manna was like white coriander seed, and its appearance was like the appearance of ice.
Did I conceive all these people, or did I give birth to them, that you say to me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries a nursing child, to the land that you swore to their fathers’?

Rather, you shall eat for a whole month, until it comes out through your nostrils and becomes bitter to you, because you rebelled against the Lord who is among you, and you wept before him and said, ‘Why did we leave Egypt?’
And Aaron said to Moses, “I beg you, my lord, do not lay sin upon us, for we acted ignorantly and sinned.”
And these are their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Salamiel son of Zaccur.
And the men who had gone with him said, “Let us not go up, for we cannot go against the nation, because it is much stronger than we are.”

And they frightened the Israelites about the land they had explored, saying, “The land through which we passed to explore it is a land that devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw in it are men of great stature.”
And each man said to his companion, “Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.”
Only do not rebel against the Lord, and do not fear the people of the land, for they are food for us. The Lord has departed from them, and the Lord is with us. Do not be afraid of them.”
And all the people said to stone them with stones, and the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud over the tent of testimony before all the Israelites.
But my servant Caleb, in whom there was a different spirit and who followed me, I will bring into the land he entered, and his descendants shall inherit it.

And you shall make a burnt offering to the Lord and a whole offering as a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering or at your festivals, to make a pleasing aroma for the Lord, whether from cattle or from the flocks.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
So that you may remember and carry out all my commandments and be holy to your God.
And the staff of the man whom I choose shall blossom, and I will remove from myself the complaints of the Israelites which they make against you.

The Lord spoke to Aaron and said, “Look, I have given you charge of my firstfruits, from everything the Israelites dedicate to me. I have given them to you as an honor, and to your sons after you, as an everlasting statute.”

“Everything that opens the womb among all flesh, which they offer to the Lord, whether human or animal, shall be yours. But you must redeem the firstborn of humans, and you must redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.”

“The Levites themselves shall perform the service of the tent of testimony, and they shall bear their sins. This is an everlasting statute throughout their generations, and they shall inherit no inheritance among the Israelites.”
Whoever comes near the corpse of any human being shall be unclean for seven days.
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went with [?] in their hands. They came to Balaam and told him Balak’s message.
God said to Balaam, “Do not go with them, and do not curse the people, because they are blessed.”
When the donkey saw the angel of God, it pressed itself against the wall and crushed Balaam’s foot, and he beat it again.
Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would have struck you by now.”
God opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the Lord blocking his way on the road, with a drawn sword in his hand. He fell on his face and bowed down to him.
When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the city of Moab, which is on the border of the Arnon, at the edge of the territory.
God appeared to Balaam, and Balaam said to him, “I have prepared seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.”
He returned to him, and he was standing beside his burnt offering, with all the rulers of Moab beside him. Balak said to him, “What did the Lord say?”
When Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel, he did not go to seek omens as he usually did, but turned his face toward the wilderness.
Edom, belonging to Esau his enemy, shall become his inheritance, and Israel acted mightily.
Hezron and the clan of Hezron; Carmi and the clan of Carmi.

The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These were prominent men of the congregation, and these were the ones who rose against Moses and Aaron in the congregation of Korah, which rose in opposition to the Lord.
These are the clans of Simeon, numbering twenty-two thousand two hundred in their census.
The sons of Issachar according to their clans: Tola and the clan of Tola; Puah and the clan of Puah; Jashub and the clan of Jashub.
These are the clans of Issachar, numbering sixty-four thousand three hundred in their census.
The name of Asher’s daughter was Serah.
The sons of Naphtali according to their clans: Jahzeel and the clan of Jahzeel; Guni and the clan of Guni.
“The daughters of Zelophehad have spoken rightly. You must give them property as an inheritance among their father’s brothers, and transfer their father’s allotted share to them.”
“May the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over this congregation.”
“You shall say to them: These are the offerings that you shall present to the Lord: two lambs without blemish every day, as a continual burnt offering.”
And a tenth for each lamb of the seven lambs.
On the first day, you shall offer burnt offerings, gifts of a pleasing aroma to the Lord: thirteen young bulls from the herd, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs. They shall be without blemish.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offerings and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides their regular burnt offerings and their drink offerings.

But if her father does not consent on the day he hears of it, none of her vows or the obligations she has imposed on herself shall stand. The Lord shall release her from guilt, because her father did not consent.

But if her husband annuls them on the day he hears of them, nothing that has come from her lips concerning her vows or the obligations she has imposed on herself shall be binding on her, because her husband has canceled them. The Lord shall release her from guilt.
Moses said to them, “Why have you kept all the females alive?”
You shall take a tribute for the Lord from all the warriors who went out to battle: one in every five hundred, from the people, the livestock, the cattle, the sheep, and the goats.
The people numbered sixteen thousand, and the tribute to the Lord from them was thirty-two people.
And thirty thousand five hundred donkeys.
And sixteen thousand people.
All your armed men shall cross the Jordan before the Lord until his enemy is destroyed before him.
Your servants shall cross over, armed and equipped for battle before the Lord, as you, lord, say.
And Baal-meon, fortified all around, and Sibmah. They gave the cities they built names of their own choosing.
The Egyptians were burying all their dead whom the Lord had struck down—all the firstborn in the land of the Egyptians. The Lord had also carried out judgment against their gods.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.

Outside the city, you shall measure two thousand cubits on the eastern side, two thousand cubits on the southern side, two thousand cubits on the western side, and two thousand cubits on the northern side, with the city in the middle. These shall be the pasturelands of the cities for you.
If he pushes him out of hatred, or throws any object at him with malicious intent, and he dies,

The congregation shall rescue the killer from the avenger of blood, and the congregation shall send him back to the city of refuge where he had taken shelter. He shall live there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
For this reason, he shall live in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest. After the death of the high priest, the killer may return to the land of his own possession.
The daughters of Zelophehad did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
